newsitem.title: UK: Eurostar launches frequent traveller award scheme.
newsitem.headline: Eurostar launches frequent traveller award scheme.

text.p: Eurostar (UK), the Channel Tunnel express rail service operator, launched an incentive programme and opened a new luxury departure lounge for travellers at London's Waterloo station on Wednesday.

Under the new Frequent Traveller programme passengers will earn points for using the services between London and Brussels and Paris which can be redeemed for various goods and services from free travel on Eurostar to transatlantic airline tickets.

Eurostar (UK) has been working hard to boost traffic this year since the British arm of the joint venture with France and Belgium's national railways was sold by the British government to the London and Continental Railways (L&CR) consortium.

L&CR has said it needs to boost traffic to over 10 million passengers a year if it is to fund the service's planned three billion-pound fast rail link from London to the Channel Tunnel, which it is has pledged to build by the year 2003.
Frequent Traveller members will be awarded points depending on what class they travel. They will get 150 points for a one-way ticket in Premium First class and 50 points for Business Standard.

Members will be issued a card which they can pass through automatic card readers in any of the three city terminals to find out how many points they have earned. Eurostar will also send customers a statement every two months.

The number of points will determine the award category, Blue for a new applicant, Silver for passengers who have collected 1,200 points over a single year, and Gold for those who have collected 2,400 points.

"The speed of redemption and generous range of rewards and benefits will make Eurostar Frequent Traveller yet another reason for travellers to turn to Eurostar," said Eurostar (UK)'s deputy chairman Adam Mills.

Eurostar (UK)'s commercial director Ian Brooks told Reuters on Wednesday that demand was currently running at a rate of 6.4 million passengers a year, up from around 3.9 million passengers a year ago.
But he estimated that Eurostar's total capacity is nearer 15 million passengers a year.
